calls.head: Power against power
calls.body: At home, the Flames keep sending Coronato’s line (Farabee, Backlund and Coronato) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Huska has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.

MIN.head: We gave Minnesota a 74% chance, but Calgary had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Flames squeak past the Wild
paras: Aydar Suniev and Joel Farabee scored power-play goals a little over three minutes apart midway through the first to put the Flames up 2-0. Michael McCarron cut Calgary’s lead to 2-1 early in the third.

The Wild had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Wild win about six in ten. Devin Cooley made the difference in net, stopping 36 of 37. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 20 of 22 for the Wild.
The Flames killed all four Wild power plays. The Wild hit three posts and came up a goal short. The Flames improved to 3-6-0, and the Wild dropped to 6-3-2.

items.text: Jonas Brodin passed Marián Gáborík for eighth on the Wild’s all-time assists list, with 219.
Kirill Kaprizov’s seven-game point streak ended.
Michael McCarron scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 13 (eleven games played since).
Maxim Shabanov was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Tyler Pitlick played instead.
